projects.title: RenewEd Tech App
projects.description: >While nearly 70% of high school students are eager to engage in environmental initiatives, only 35% feel confident using sustainable technology in their projects. I created RenewEd Tech to bridge this gap, making sustainability education approachable, engaging, and action-driven.>I developed RenewEd Tech using JavaScript, with React Native for the front end and Firebase for the backend. The app includes a chatbot powered by Google’s Gemini, trained on climate data from five U.S. states, and built in Visual Studio Code. It offers a clean, user-friendly interface with interactive lessons, quizzes, a guided chatbot, and a dynamic project task planner.>RenewEd Tech transforms students from passive learners into active changemakers. It simplifies complex environmental concepts through bite-sized lessons and empowers users to develop real-world sustainability projects in their local communities. Educators benefit from ready-to-use resources, and communities see real environmental improvements. RenewEd Tech equips the next generation with the skills, confidence, and tools to take climate action where it matters most: their communities.

Every AI wave was bottlenecked by data, then unlocked by tooling. CV had ImageNet, then Roboflow. LLMs had the internet, then RLHF. Physical AI has neither. Robot foundation models don't learn from flat images, they learn from trajectories. Synchronized video, depth, proprioception, force, language, action, all time-aligned, all embodiment-specific. Every lab that wants to train one ends up building its own teleop rig, its own storage format, its own QA pipeline from scratch. There's no ImageNet moment yet. No Roboflow moment either. That's starting to change. Formats like RLDS and Hugging Face's LeRobot are becoming the shared language, the LeRobot dataset hub went from about 1,145 datasets to over 58,000 in about a year. Open X-Embodiment is doing for manipulation data what ImageNet did for vision. The demand is showing up everywhere too. Search interest in "physical AI" is up 3.5x year over year. The pattern is the same every time. The models get good before the data infrastructure catches up. Whoever builds the layer that makes the data usable, not just another dataset host, but real tooling for ingest, annotation, and augmentation, ends up owning a foundational piece of the next decade of AI. That's what we're building at phydata. https://phydata.tech/ #PhysicalAI #AIData #RealWorldData #ArtificialIntelligence #Phydata

This past week, I had the opportunity to attend Jane Street 's WiSE program in NYC and Y Combinator 's Startup School 2026 in SF. At WiSE, I loved getting an inside look at the world of quantitative finance through panels, conversations with Jane Streeters, and playing mock trading games. I met so many girls who share my interests in math and CS - huge thank you to Katie Nasta and Kylie Newman for organizing such a engaging program! At YC Startup School, among all the spontaneous conversations I had, a few highlights included attending the Future Female Founders Summit, speaking with David S. Roberts about the AI/Biotech space and multimodal fusion during a breakout session, and learning from Gabriel Birnbaum about his work in AI-based storytelling during the career fair. As Sam Altman said, the best ideas start with believing in a possibility long before everyone else sees it. What an unforgettable week!

I spent the weekend in SF at YC Startup School learning from and connecting with people at the forefront of the startup world. Everything hit harder when Jensen Huang said this is “the greatest time in the last 60 years to start a company.” I received the motivation and resources ($25k of computing credits and a 6 month subscription to Claude Max 20x) I need to start pursuing my ideas (and some AWESOME PostHog and Google merch). I heard talks from people such as Sam Altman, Alexandr Wang , Chelsea Finn , and more. I got within two feet of Garry Tan , one of the most influential people for students like myself. Having the honor to chat with Gabriel Birnbaum about his work at Y/n and Can of Soup showed me just how many possibilities there are in the startup world. Special thank you to Nikki Kothapalli , Alison Choi , Aiden Seo , and many other fellow students with whom i had some insightful conversations and who made this week one to remember. Excited to start at MIT in August, continue building, and see what comes next!
